edits.value_json: 日 is a picture of the sun. Shang-period inscriptions also attest it for daylight and as a unit of days, without establishing which use came first.
Shang-period oracle-bone inscriptions; current Chinese use
Oracle-bone examples attest 日 for the sun, and present-day Chinese dictionaries list this sense. Its use in the earliest documented corpus cited here does not prove it was the graph's first-ever use.
Shang-period oracle-bone inscriptions; current Chinese use

Oracle-bone examples use 日 for daylight, including in contrast with evening, and a present-day Chinese dictionary lists daytime as a sense. The evidence does not establish whether this use developed from the sun sense.
Shang-period oracle-bone inscriptions; current Chinese use

An oracle-bone example attests 日 for a five-day period, and present-day Chinese dictionaries list day as a calendrical unit. The evidence does not establish when or how this use relates to the sun and daylight uses.
